key_insight: The Large Cancer Assistant (LCA) separates clinical orchestration from AI inference, enabling model-agnostic and scalable oncology decision support.
engineering_relevance: Its architecture is relevant for building robust hospital AI pipelines because it decouples multimodal data routing, model execution, and infrastructure integration.
method: Formalizes LCA as a 7-tuple orchestration architecture with algorithmic impermeability.
Uses an Entry Theory based on geometric deep learning to standardize multimodal patient data.
Routes cases through a Cancer Switching Module and outputs a Standardized Intermediate Payload (SIP) for downstream processing.
evidence_signal: A proof-of-concept tested four technical scenarios and reported negligible orchestration overhead, invariant routing under model swaps, 100% recall for supplementary data requests under anomalies, and successful multi-protocol execution.
watch_item: The framework appears validated only at proof-of-concept scale, so real-world clinical integration, interoperability, and operational reliability still need broader evaluation.
paper_title: The Large Cancer Assistant (LCA): A Model-Agnostic Orchestration Framework for Scalable Clinical Decision Support in Oncology
